pointers.sentence: `View` is the base class of the generic views and of every view made with `as_view`, and it is small: it dispatches by HTTP method and makes a few checks (`django/views/generic/base.py:View`).

The handler wants one callable that serves every request, and `as_view` gives it one that makes an instance for each, so that each request has state of its own and a handler method may keep what it likes on `self` (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.as_view`).

`as_view` is a `classonlymethod`, a `classmethod` that raises `AttributeError` when it is looked up on an instance, so it can be called on the class and on nothing else (`django/utils/decorators.py:classonlymethod`).
It refuses any name that is not already an attribute of the class, so a misspelt name raises as the URLconf is imported (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.as_view`).

If `View.view_is_async` finds the class's handler methods to be coroutine functions, the function is marked as one too ([Asynchronous views](async.md#a-class-whose-handler-methods-are-coroutines)) (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.as_view`).

`as_view` leaves the two names alone and records the class in `"view_class"`, and where `ResolverMatch` keeps a dotted path for a view it reads the class from there in the function's place (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.as_view`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:ResolverMatch.__init__`).

`as_view` leaves the two names alone and records the class in `"view_class"`, and where `ResolverMatch` keeps a dotted path for a view it reads the class from there in the function's place (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.as_view`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:ResolverMatch.__init__`).
It holds the instance only in a local variable, so once it has returned, the function no longer holds the instance (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.as_view`).
Django's documentation warns against passing a list, a dictionary or any other mutable object to a view for that reason (`docs/ref/class-based-views/index.txt`).
What belongs to one request is what a method assigns on `self` (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.as_view`).

Other methods read them from there: `SingleObjectMixin.get_object` reads the slug from `kwargs` without being passed it (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.setup`, `django/views/generic/detail.py:SingleObjectMixin.get_object`).

Other methods read them from there: `SingleObjectMixin.get_object` reads the slug from `kwargs` without being passed it (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.setup`, `django/views/generic/detail.py:SingleObjectMixin.get_object`).

Between `setup` and `dispatch` the function checks that the instance has a `request`, and if it has none, raises an `AttributeError` that asks whether `setup` was overridden without a call to `super()` (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.as_view`).

`setup` is a hook of its own so that a class can prepare, before `dispatch` runs, what all of its handler methods share: the function calls it on each new instance, with the request and its arguments, before it calls `dispatch` (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.as_view`).
In every other case it is `View.http_method_not_allowed` (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.dispatch`).

`"HEAD"` found the one `setup` added, and `"OPTIONS"` finds `View.options`, which `View` supplies for every class: an empty 200 response with an `"Allow"` header and a `Content-Length` of zero (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.options`).

`dispatch` then calls `View.http_method_not_allowed`, which logs a warning to `"django.request"` and returns an `HttpResponseNotAllowed`, a 405 with the same `"Allow"` header, from inside a coroutine if `View.view_is_async` finds the class asynchronous, as `View.options` does ([Asynchronous views](async.md#a-class-whose-handler-methods-are-coroutines)) (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.http_method_not_allowed`).

A handler method the class defines is then unreachable if its name is not in the list, because `dispatch` tests the list before it looks at the instance (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.dispatch`).

A decorator written for function views, applied to `dispatch` through `method_decorator`, covers every handler method at once, which is how Django's own `LoginView` is decorated ([Decorating a class: `method_decorator`](method-decorator.md)) (`django/utils/decorators.py:method_decorator`, `django/contrib/auth/views.py:LoginView`).

A mixin that decides whether the request may proceed overrides `dispatch`, makes its test, and calls `super().dispatch` only if the test passes, as `LoginRequiredMixin` does, answering a user who is not logged in through `AccessMixin.handle_no_permission` ([Requiring a login: `login_required`, `permission_required` and `LoginRequiredMiddleware`](../auth/requiring-login.md#the-mixins-and-accessmixinhandle_no_permission)) (`django/contrib/auth/mixins.py:LoginRequiredMixin.dispatch`).
